songInfo.title: Sunday Bloody Sunday
songInfo.tuning: Half-Step Down (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)

scalesUsed.notes: B - C# - D - E - F# - G - A
scalesUsed.application: Drives the somber, brooding verses and the signature arpeggiated intro progression (Bm - D - G)

scalesUsed.notes: D - E - F# - G - A - B - C#
scalesUsed.application: Relative major key providing the emotional lift and defiance in the chorus and bridge
Underpins The Edge's clean melodic stabs, natural harmonics, and dramatic solo interlude

keyAndScale.keySignature: Two sharps (F#, C#) (concert Bb minor due to half-step down tuning)
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: B Minor is the relative minor of D Major

mainProgression.description: The quintessential post-punk anthemic progression. The Edge voices the chords with open ringing high strings (open B and high E), picking ascending triads that are rhythmically multiplied by a precise 364ms dotted-eighth digital delay.

sectionProgressions.section: Signature Intro Arpeggio & Military Drum Beat
sectionProgressions.description: Larry Mullen Jr.'s iconic military marching snare groove paired with The Edge's echoing arpeggiated triads
Intense, repetitive arpeggio pattern maintaining tension beneath Bono's passionate vocal delivery
'Sunday, Bloody Sunday!' - full open chords ring out as the song shifts toward the relative major key of D
Dramatic breakdown featuring sparkling natural harmonics on frets 7 and 12 over a descending bassline

harmonicFunction: Bm (i) - Dark, brooding tonic minor chord setting the solemn political and historical gravity
D (bIII) - Relative major chord injecting hope, defiance, and melodic brightness
G6 (bVI) - Submediant chord made expansive by open ringing B and E strings
A (bVII) - Subtonic chord providing forward momentum in the bridge turnaround

techniques.name: Dotted-Eighth Rhythmic Delay Interplay
techniques.description: Setting a digital delay unit to a precise dotted-eighth note value (364ms at 103 BPM) and playing steady eighth notes, allowing the repeats to slot into the sixteenth-note gaps for a cascading rhythmic wall of sound

notes: Tune your delay pedal to 364 milliseconds (or tap tempo with dotted-eighth subdivision)
Set delay feedback to roughly 3-4 clean repeats and mix/level to approximately 50-60%
Pick straight down-up eighth notes strictly on the beat
Do not rush: let the delay repeats do the heavy lifting to create the driving sixteenth-note gallop
sequence: Fret Bm triad shape on strings 4, 3, and 2
Pick strings 3 and 2 ascendingly, letting open high E ring freely
Listen to the echo repeat fall precisely halfway between your pick strokes
tips: Use a Fender Stratocaster in the 'in-between' pickup positions (position 2: bridge + middle) for classic 'quack' and high-end chime
Use a Herdim plectrum held sideways with the dimpled grip edge striking the string for The Edge's signature rasping attack
Always practice with a metronome or drum machine to lock in with the delay tempo

techniques.name: Natural Harmonic Bell Chimes
techniques.description: Lightly touching string nodes directly above the 7th and 12th fretwires with fret-hand fingertips while picking sharply, producing crystalline bell-like tones that echo through the delay pedal

notes: Position your fret-hand finger lightly on the string directly above the fretwire, not behind the fret
Strike the string with a firm pick attack close to the bridge
Lift your fret-hand finger off the string immediately upon picking to allow the harmonic to ring
Let the delay and reverb sustain the chime into a lush ambient pad
sequence: Lightly touch string 1 directly above fret 12
Pick with downstroke, lifting finger instantly
Move down to fret 7 on strings 2 and 3, picking in sequence
Allow the repeats to interweave with the acoustic drum beat
tips: Ensure your fingernails don't touch the string; use only the soft pad of your finger
Roll off bass on your amplifier to keep harmonic highs crystalline and focused
Add a subtle touch of analog chorus to give the chime stereo width

sections.name: Intro Military Drum & Echoing Arpeggio
sections.description: Larry Mullen Jr.'s famous martial snare beat introduces the track before The Edge's razor-sharp Stratocaster arpeggio enters with 364ms dotted-eighth delay at 103 BPM.
notes: Play straight eighth notes without rushing
Allow the open high E and B strings to ring continuously
Keep pick attack sharp and uniform using a dimpled nylon pick
Let the delay repeats double the rhythmic density

sections.name: Verse 1 Rhythmic Pulse
sections.description: 'I can't believe the news today...' - Bono's impassioned vocal enters over the hypnotic, circular arpeggio cadence.
notes: Strict dynamic discipline behind the vocal phrases
Mute strings slightly during the transitions between Bm and D
Accentuate downbeats to keep time with the bass drum
Let the open G6 chord ring to create harmonic space

sections.name: Chorus Stadium Defiance
sections.description: 'Sunday, Bloody Sunday!' - full open major chords ring out in triumph and protest, sweeping across D and G.
notes: Strum full open D and G cowboy chords with wide dynamic swings
Hit the upbeat strums firmly to excite the delay repeats
Electric violin and backing vocal counterpoint enter the mix
Crisp transition back to the arpeggio motif on the turnaround

sections.name: Bridge Natural Harmonics Breakdown
sections.description: 'And the battle's just begun, there's many lost, but tell me who has won?' - sparse acoustic breakdown featuring sparkling natural harmonics.
notes: Touch fretwire 12 lightly on strings 1, 2, and 3
Play natural harmonics on fret 7 for high bell-like ringing
Allow the delay repeats to wash across the martial snare rhythm
Build dynamic intensity toward the electric guitar solo

sections.name: Guitar Solo & High Register Fanfare
sections.description: The Edge plays a fierce, soaring melodic solo high on the fretboard, utilizing octave leaps and rhythmic single-note pulses.
notes: Target the high D note on fret 10 of the high E string
Execute rapid eighth-note tremolo picking augmented by the delay pedal
Slide down with dramatic pick scrape
Resolve cleanly into the final triumphant chorus
sections.exerciseLabel: High Register Melodic Solo & Delay Tremolo Study

sections.name: Outro Climax & Final Resolving Chords
sections.description: Final repetition of the signature arpeggio riff punctuated by military drum rolls, fading into a single ringing natural harmonic.
notes: Lock seamlessly with Mullen's fading snare pattern
Let the final chord ring out naturally into silence
Strum final Bm triad with warm tube sustain
End on a lone high E natural harmonic at fret 12

guitar.recommended: Fender Stratocaster (1970s black Strat with maple neck)
guitar.pickup: Bridge/middle 'in-between' position (position 2) for glassy, hollow chime

amp.recommended: Vox AC30 Top Boost pushed into warm edge-of-breakup saturation
alternatives: Boss Katana 100 (Clean Channel with Treble Boost)

effects.distortion: Electro-Harmonix Memory Man preamp boost or Ibanez TS9 Tube Screamer set low
effects.reverb: Spring reverb from the Vox AC30 (1.5s decay)
effects.other: Electro-Harmonix Deluxe Memory Man or Korg SDD-3000 digital delay set to 364ms (dotted-eighth) with 3-4 repeats

beginner.title: Open Chords & Strumming Pattern
steps: Tune your guitar half-step down (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)
Learn open Bm, D, G, and A chord fingerings
Practice transitioning between Bm and D in time at 103 BPM

intermediate.title: Dotted-Eighth Delay Synchronization
steps: Set up your delay pedal to exactly 364ms with 3 repeats
Practice playing straight eighth-note arpeggios against the delay pulse
Master the open ringing high strings (B and high E) during chord shifts

advanced.title: Natural Harmonics, Solo & Complete Performance
steps: Execute the crystalline natural harmonics on frets 7 and 12 with precision
Perform the high-register solo fanfare with alternate picking
Play along with the complete 4:39 track maintaining lockstep tempo with the drums

commonMistakes: Playing in standard tuning instead of tuning down a half-step (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)
Setting the delay time to a quarter note instead of a precise dotted-eighth note (364ms at 103 BPM)
Playing too many notes with the pick hand instead of letting the delay repeats fill the rhythmic spaces
Fretting natural harmonics too firmly, preventing the harmonic node from sounding
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: Half-step down tuning check and gentle finger warm-up
10 mins: Slow metronome practice of the main arpeggio with delay engaged at 80, 95, and 103 BPM
10 mins: Natural harmonic accuracy drills across frets 7 and 12
10 mins: Full rhythm play-through focusing on chorus dynamic transitions
focusAreas: Precise delay tempo synchronization and pick attack consistency
Clean execution of natural harmonics at frets 7 and 12
Dynamic control between introspective verses and stadium choruses
metronomeWork: Set your metronome to 103 BPM and lock in your delay pedal's tap tempo
Practice picking strictly on the click; any timing rush will cause delay repeats to clash
Isolate the Bm to D transition until the chord shift occurs without missing an eighth note

sameArtist.title: Where the Streets Have No Name
sameArtist.similarity: The Edge's definitive dotted-eighth delay arpeggio masterpiece in D Major
